corrections.why: NH48 places the peak in Grafton County within the Bethlehem area; the FFLA listing says Coos. Check against a county map before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The White Mountain History article says steel; NH48 says wooden with a warden's cabin. No source settles it, so the story reports both.
NH48 says 1948; the 1HappyHiker blog and the Weirs Times (citing the FFLA site) say 1950. Both dates are reported.
FFLA lists Coos; NH48 lists Grafton. The story reports both and flags the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Built year and tower removal (1929, 1972) agree across four sources. The material, the 1948 vs 1950 closing date and the county are in real conflict. The NHHS photos of the Hale tower (objects 288992 and 288964, dated 23 September 1929) are real finds, but the cached pages carry no description or licence text, so no photo is added; check the licence before adding them. The 2016 blog description of a tree-enclosed corral was seen only in a search snippet and is not quoted.
